extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents/attorneys, and USPTO examiners handling PCT national stage entry into the U.S.
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for entering an international (PCT) application into the U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, including claim amendments, fees, translations, inventor oaths/declarations, applicant identity, and related documentary requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendment: complete claim listing
rubrics_metrics.description: One requirement for effectively amending claims in a national phase application is a complete listing of all claims ever presented, including the text of all pending and withdrawn claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The status of every claim in such listing must be indicated after its claim number by a parenthetical identifier (see next metric). For the manner and required format of making amendments, consult 37 CFR 1.121 and 1.125. The Office may waive certain provisions of 37 CFR 1.121 and accept alternative status identifiers in some cases (see MPEP §714 II.C item (E)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim status identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim in the complete listing must include one of the following identifiers in a parenthetical expression: (Original), (Currently Amended), (Canceled), (Withdrawn), (Previously Presented), (New), and (Not Entered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative status identifiers set forth in MPEP §714 II.C item (E) will be accepted if the amendment otherwise complies with 37 CFR 1.121. Examples in the MPEP show correct usage for claims affected by PCT Article 19/34 filings (see provided examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings for currently amended claims
rubrics_metrics.description: All 'currently amended' claims must include markings to indicate the changes made relative to the immediate prior version of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use underlining to indicate additions and strike-through or double brackets for deletions (see 37 CFR 1.121(c) for further details regarding format). Markings must reflect changes relative to the immediate prior version.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use 'original', 'previously presented', and 'cancelled'
rubrics_metrics.description: The status identifier 'original' must be used for claims that had been presented on the international filing date and not modified or canceled; 'previously presented' is used for claims added or modified under PCT Articles 19 or 34 in the international phase that were subsequently entered in the national phase; 'canceled' is used for claims canceled under a PCT Article 19 or 34 amendment in the international phase and subsequently entered in the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP provides concrete examples (Example 1–4) illustrating how to label claim statuses after Article 19/34 filings and renumberings. Follow those examples to avoid mislabeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant claim amendments will not be entered
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments that are not submitted in compliance with the applicable regulations will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, submission with the national stage documents of a revised set of claims, absent a preliminary amendment to the claims in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(c), will not be effective to amend the claims of record in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant identity: who may be applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'applicant' and who may apply for a U.S. patent: the inventor(s), legal representative of a deceased/incapacitated inventor, assignee, obligated assignee, or a person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest (depending on filing date and statute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.42, 1.43, 1.45, and 1.46. The America Invents Act (AIA) expanded who may be an applicant for national stage applications with international filing dates on or after September 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) when applicant is not the inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application under 35 U.S.C. 111 is made by a person other than the inventor under §1.46, the application must contain an application data sheet under §1.76 specifying in the applicant information section the assignee or other person identified as applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a non-inventor applies in the national stage, that person should normally have been identified as the applicant for the United States in the international stage; documentary evidence of ownership for an assignee should be recorded no later than issue fee payment (part 3). A person showing sufficient proprietary interest must submit a petition including the fee (37 CFR 1.17(g)), a showing of sufficient proprietary interest, and a statement that their action preserves parties' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction or change of applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to correct or update the name of the applicant or to change the applicant after an original applicant has been specified must include an application data sheet under §1.76 specifying the correct or updated name and comply with applicable provisions (e.g., §1.76(c)(2), §§3.71 and 3.73).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A change in the applicant under 37 CFR 1.46(c)(2) requires an ADS specifying the applicant in the applicant information section and compliance with petition/statement requirements where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic national fee timing (30 months) — non-extendable
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic national fee must be paid prior to the expiration of 30 months from the priority date to avoid abandonment of the international application as to the United States; this time period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contrasts with U.S. national filings under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) where certain fees may be accepted later with a surcharge. Consult the Official Gazette for current fee listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of payments when fees insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: If fees have been paid in a national stage application prior to 30 months but the applicant has not specified a sufficient amount for the basic national fee, the Office will apply the payment first to the basic national fee regardless of applicant's specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful when specifying fee allocations; the Office's priority is to apply payments to the basic national fee to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which fee regulations apply (37 CFR 1.16 vs 1.492)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees under 37 CFR 1.16 relate to national applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), not to international applications entering the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371; national stage fees are provided in 37 CFR 1.492.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, an authorization to charge fees under 37 CFR 1.16 in an international application entering the national stage will be treated as an authorization to charge fees under 37 CFR 1.492 (see 37 CFR 1.25(b)). Applications will not be held abandoned if an authorization to charge fees under 1.16 has been provided instead of 1.492.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of preliminary amendment on extra claim fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment accompanying the initial national stage submission that is effective to cancel claims and/or eliminate multiple dependent claims will be effective to reduce the number of claims considered in calculating extra claim fees and/or eliminate multiple dependent claim fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A subsequently filed amendment canceling claims or eliminating multiple dependent claims will not entitle applicant to a refund of fees previously paid. See MPEP §§607 and 608.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The application size fee for a national stage application (37 CFR 1.492(j)) is determined on the basis of the international application as published by WIPO pursuant to PCT Article 21.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculation is based on number of sheets of specification (description, claims, abstract, and, if present, a sequence listing in PDF) and drawings in the published international application, without regard to publication language. Certain sheets (Article 19 amendments/statement, international search report, additional bibliographic sheets other than the cover sheet with the abstract) are not counted. Article 34 amendments or preliminary amendments are not taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and surcharge fees for late submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A processing fee (37 CFR 1.492(i)) is required for acceptance of an English translation of the international application later than 30 months from the priority date; a surcharge fee (37 CFR 1.492(h)) is required for acceptance of any of the search fee, examination fee, or inventor's oath or declaration after the date of commencement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission avoids these additional fees. See 37 CFR 1.492 provisions for amounts and application.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation requirement and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants entering the national stage in the U.S. must file an English translation of the international application if the international application was filed in another language and was not published under PCT Article 21(2) in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international filing dates on or after July 1, 2022, an English translation is required for any Sequence Listing XML that contains non-English language-dependent free text qualifiers (see 37 CFR 1.831–1.834). A translation must be of the international application as filed or with changes properly accepted under PCT Rule 26 or rectifications under PCT Rule 91; partial translations or translations that include unauthorized modifications are unacceptable. Words in drawings must be furnished as new drawings or copies with the translation pasted on the original text (PCT Rule 49.5(d)). Amendments may not be incorporated into the translation; amend under 37 CFR 1.121 and generally within applicable time limits (e.g., within 3 months from national stage entry per 37 CFR 1.491).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and time to correct missing/defective translation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the translation is missing or defective after timely payment of basic national fee and submission of copy of international application, the Office will send a Notification of Missing Requirements (PCT/DO/EO/905) setting a period to correct missing or defective requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time period is 32 months from the priority date or 2 months from the date of the notice, whichever expires later. That period may be extended up to five additional months as provided in 37 CFR 1.136(a). A processing fee is required for accepting a translation after 30 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT publication translation obligations (PCT Rule 48.3(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to PCT Rule 48.3(c), if the international application is published in a language other than English, the publication shall include an English translation of the title of the invention, the abstract, and any text matter pertaining to the figure(s) accompanying the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such translations are prepared under the responsibility of the International Bureau and are part of the published international application record used for national stage calculations/requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation relied on for provisional rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A translation of the international application as filed and identified as provided in 37 CFR 1.417 submitted for the purpose of obtaining provisional rights pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 154(d)(4) can be relied on to fulfill the translation requirement under 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(2) in a national stage application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the translation submitted for provisional rights meets the translation completeness and accuracy requirements described elsewhere (cannot incorporate unauthorized amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's oath or declaration required (35 U.S.C. 371(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(4), the applicant for a national stage application is required to file an oath or declaration of the inventor (or other person authorized under chapter 11) complying with the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 115 and with regulations prescribed for oaths or declarations of applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements differ depending on international filing date (pre- vs post-AIA). For international filing dates on or after September 16, 2012, 37 CFR 1.497 applies: an inventor's oath/declaration will be accepted as complying with 371(c)(4) if it complies with 37 CFR 1.63(a),(c),(g) (or substitute statement under 1.64 meeting specified requirements); if not, outstanding requirements must be satisfied. If a declaration in compliance with 1.63 was previously submitted in the international phase under PCT Rule 4.17(iv) within PCT Rule 26ter.1 time limits, a new filing may not be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponement and timing rules for inventor's oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of the inventor's oath or declaration may be postponed until the application is otherwise in condition for allowance if the applicant submits an application data sheet identifying each inventor by legal name, mailing address, and residence as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postponement under 37 CFR 1.495(c) does not postpone the requirement to pay the surcharge fee for filing the oath/declaration after commencement. All required oaths/declarations or substitute statements must be filed prior to or with a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114. Early national stage entry under 35 U.S.C. 371(f) requires submission of the oath or declaration and that submission may not be postponed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and consequence for missing oath/declaration or ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: If the basic national fee and copy of the international application have been received by 30 months but the required inventor's oath or declaration or an application data sheet under 37 CFR 1.495(c)(3) has not been submitted, the Office will send a Notification of Missing Requirements (PCT/DO/EO/905) setting a time period to submit the required documents and surcharge fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file the required reply will result in abandonment of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship determination and corrections for national stage entry
rubrics_metrics.description: For international applications entering the national stage on or after September 16, 2012, the inventorship is the inventor(s) set forth in the application data sheet filed with the initial 371 submission; if no ADS is filed, inventorship is that set forth in the international application (including changes under PCT Rule 92bis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventorship may be corrected under 37 CFR 1.48(a); the name of an inventor may be corrected or updated under 1.48(f). If an inventor is deceased, incapacitated, refuses to execute the oath, or cannot be found after diligent effort, a substitute statement under 37 CFR 1.64 may be submitted in lieu of an oath or declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA (pre‑Sept 16, 2012) oath/declaration rules and changes of inventive entity
rubrics_metrics.description: For international filing dates before September 16, 2012, pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.497 applies: an oath/declaration must be executed in accordance with 1.66 or 1.68, identify the specification, identify each inventor and country of citizenship, and state belief that the named inventor(s) are original and first inventor(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an oath/declaration filed pursuant to pre‑AIA 1.497 names an inventive entity different from that in the international application, applicant must submit statements from added/deleted inventors that any error occurred without deceptive intent, pay processing fee (1.17(i)), provide assignee consent if needed, and possibly file a new oath/declaration. The Office may require other information; changes to inventorship effected under PCT Rule 92bis or corrections to priority claims may require new oaths or ADSs.
